column3: The historical present is rendered in the past.
“People ... from” makes the place names’ inhabitants explicit.
The confession is moved before the baptism.
“John” supplies the subject; “place of baptism” interprets “his baptism.”
The cutting and throwing are expressed in the future.
The two future actions become purposes introduced by “to.”
The historical present is rendered in the past.
“John” makes the subject explicit; the final historical present becomes past.
“To Him” is not expressed; “resting” interprets coming upon Him.
